lessons.title: Bienvenue dans notre laboratoire scientifique
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify the classroom science area as a special place for discovery and learning

opening.activity: Science area tour - students explore and touch safe science materials while teacher narrates
opening.visualSupports: colorful science area label with pictures of tools and discoveries

main.activity: hands-on exploration of science tools and materials with guided discovery questions
main.visualSupports: picture cards showing scientists at work, lab safety symbols

decisionPoints.question: Are students excited about the science tools and asking questions?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Let them handle tools briefly with safety reminders
decisionPoints.ifNo: Model exciting discoveries you can make with each tool

closing.activity: Circle discussion - students share what they're most excited to discover in our science area

troubleshooting.then: Show pictures of real scientists and compare them to students: 'You are scientists when you explore and discover!'

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding that scientists work in special places with special tools, just like doctors or chefs

lessons.title: Nos règles de sécurité en sciences
lessons.oneGoal: Students will learn and practice three basic safety rules for science activities: listen, look, and be careful

opening.activity: Safety song with actions - teaching three key safety moves: hands on ears (listen), hand over eyes (look), gentle hands (be careful)
opening.visualSupports: three large safety rule pictures with simple symbols

main.activity: safety practice scenarios where students demonstrate listening, looking carefully, and being gentle with science materials
main.visualSupports: safety rule reminder chart visible during all activities

decisionPoints.question: Can students demonstrate the three safety rules consistently?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Practice with actual science materials
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use role-play with stuffed animals or puppets to show safe vs unsafe behaviors

closing.activity: Safety promise circle - each student practices one safety rule and makes a promise to stay safe

troubleshooting.then: Start with just 'listen' rule and add others gradually over several lessons

lessons.realWorldConnection: Learning that safety rules help us have fun and stay safe, like wearing seatbelts in cars

lessons.title: Observer avec nos yeux de scientifiques
lessons.oneGoal: Students will practice careful observation skills using only their eyes to notice details about objects

opening.activity: Eye spy science game - students find objects with specific characteristics using only their eyes
opening.visualSupports: poster showing different observation words: big, small, shiny, rough

main.activity: detailed observation practice with mystery objects in bags - students describe what they see without touching
main.visualSupports: observation vocabulary chart with pictures, 'scientist eyes' poster

decisionPoints.question: Can students describe multiple details about objects using observation words?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Challenge them to notice tiny details or compare two similar objects
decisionPoints.ifNo: Model observation by thinking aloud about one object together

closing.activity: Observation sharing - students tell partners about the most interesting detail they noticed

troubleshooting.then: Give sentence starters: 'I see that it is...' or 'This object looks...'

lessons.realWorldConnection: Using careful looking to notice things around us, like watching for changes in the weather

lessons.title: Écouter comme des scientifiques
lessons.oneGoal: Students will use their sense of hearing to gather information about different objects and materials

opening.activity: Sound detective game - students close eyes and identify familiar classroom sounds
opening.visualSupports: poster showing different sound words: loud, quiet, high, low

main.activity: sound exploration stations where students safely shake, tap, and drop different materials to compare sounds
main.visualSupports: sound comparison chart, listening rules poster

decisionPoints.question: Can students describe differences between sounds using sound vocabulary?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Have them predict what sounds different materials will make
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on simple loud/quiet comparisons with clear examples

closing.activity: Sound symphony - students create patterns with their favorite sound-makers from the lesson

troubleshooting.then: Use comparative language: 'This sounds more like...' or 'Which is louder?'

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding how listening carefully helps us learn, like hearing if something is working properly

lessons.title: Sentir en sécurité
lessons.oneGoal: Students will learn when and how to safely use their sense of smell in science investigations

opening.activity: Safe smelling demonstration - teacher shows proper 'wafting' technique with pleasant scents
opening.visualSupports: step-by-step safe smelling poster with hand gestures

main.activity: guided scent exploration with teacher-prepared safe containers and practice of safe smelling technique
materials: scent containers with vanilla, lemon, cinnamon
main.visualSupports: smell safety rules chart, scent description word wall

decisionPoints.question: Are students using safe smelling technique consistently?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Let them explore different scents and describe what they smell
decisionPoints.ifNo: Practice wafting technique with unscented containers first

closing.activity: Scent memory game - students match pleasant scents they explored and discuss safety rules

troubleshooting.then: Practice with empty containers and emphasize 'gentle waving' motion

lessons.realWorldConnection: Learning that some smells tell us about safety, like smelling food to know if it's fresh

lessons.title: Toucher avec précaution
lessons.oneGoal: Students will learn safe touching techniques for science exploration and when NOT to touch

opening.activity: Touch safety demonstration using 'one finger first' rule and identifying no-touch items
opening.visualSupports: safe touching rules poster with pictures, red 'no-touch' symbols

main.activity: texture exploration stations with various safe materials and practice of gentle touching techniques
main.visualSupports: texture vocabulary chart with feeling words, safe touch reminder signs

decisionPoints.question: Are students using gentle touch and following 'one finger first' rule?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Challenge them to find textures that are similar or completely different
decisionPoints.ifNo: Model gentle touching with a puppet or stuffed animal first

closing.activity: Texture guessing game - students describe how materials feel without naming them

troubleshooting.then: Practice 'butterfly touches' - gentle like a butterfly landing on a flower

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding when it's safe to touch things and when we need to be careful, like petting friendly animals

lessons.title: Nos outils de scientifiques
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify and name basic science tools: magnifying glass, ruler, and measuring cups

opening.activity: Science tool mystery box - students guess tools by feeling them and discussing their uses
opening.visualSupports: large tool identification poster with names and pictures

main.activity: hands-on tool exploration where students practice holding and using each tool safely with teacher guidance
main.visualSupports: tool safety rules chart, proper holding technique pictures

decisionPoints.question: Can students hold tools safely and name them correctly?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Let them practice using tools with interesting objects
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on one tool at a time with lots of modeling and practice

closing.activity: Tool match game - students match tool names to pictures and share which tool they're most excited to use

troubleshooting.then: Create simple rhymes or songs for each tool: 'Loupe helps me see, tiny things clearly!'

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding that scientists use special tools to see and measure better, like how doctors use stethoscopes

lessons.title: Explorer avec une loupe
lessons.oneGoal: Students will use magnifying glasses safely to observe small details in familiar objects

opening.activity: Magnifying glass magic - teacher demonstrates amazing details visible through magnification
opening.visualSupports: magnifying glass safety rules poster with pictures

main.activity: guided magnifying exploration of classroom objects with focus on discovering new details and safe handling
main.visualSupports: detail discovery chart, safe magnifying technique posters

decisionPoints.question: Are students discovering new details and using magnifiers safely?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Challenge them to compare details between similar objects
decisionPoints.ifNo: Provide easier objects with obvious details and model proper magnifying technique

closing.activity: Amazing discoveries sharing - students share the coolest detail they discovered through magnification

troubleshooting.then: Help them find the right distance by moving slowly closer and farther from objects

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding how magnifying glasses help us see tiny things, like looking at insects or reading small print

lessons.title: Mesurer avec des outils
lessons.oneGoal: Students will use simple measuring tools to compare sizes and amounts of classroom objects

opening.activity: Size comparison game - students order objects by size using their hands and eyes before using tools
opening.visualSupports: size comparison vocabulary poster: bigger, smaller, same size

main.activity: measurement exploration stations using non-standard (blocks, hands) and standard tools (rulers) to compare object sizes
main.visualSupports: measurement technique posters, comparison language chart

decisionPoints.question: Can students use measuring tools to compare objects accurately?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Have them predict measurements before testing and compare predictions to results
decisionPoints.ifNo: Start with non-standard units (blocks, hands) and focus on 'longer/shorter' comparisons

closing.activity: Measurement discoveries - students share surprising measurement discoveries and demonstrate measuring techniques

troubleshooting.then: Start with measuring in blocks or hands first, then gradually introduce ruler use

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding how we measure things in daily life, like checking if clothes fit or measuring ingredients

lessons.title: Dessiner nos observations
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create simple drawings to record what they observe during science investigations

opening.activity: Scientist drawing demonstration - teacher shows how scientists draw what they see, not what they think
opening.visualSupports: scientific drawing rules poster: draw what you see, include details, use labels

main.activity: guided observation drawing practice with real objects, focusing on accuracy and detail recording
main.visualSupports: scientific drawing examples, observation vocabulary for labeling

decisionPoints.question: Are students drawing what they actually see rather than what they know?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage them to add labels and more details to their drawings
decisionPoints.ifNo: Cover the object and uncover it gradually, drawing each part as they see it

closing.activity: Drawing gallery walk - students display their observation drawings and explain what details they included

troubleshooting.then: Start with simple shapes and add one detail at a time: 'First draw the shape, then add the color'

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding that scientists keep track of what they discover by drawing, like how we draw pictures of family trips

lessons.title: Trier et classer nos découvertes
lessons.oneGoal: Students will sort objects into groups based on observable characteristics like color, size, or texture

opening.activity: Sorting game with students - teacher sorts students by clothing colors, then students suggest other sorting rules
opening.visualSupports: sorting rules poster with pictures showing different ways to group objects

main.activity: hands-on sorting activities where students classify objects multiple ways and explain their sorting decisions
main.visualSupports: classification vocabulary chart, sorting strategy posters

decisionPoints.question: Can students sort objects consistently using observable characteristics?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Challenge them to re-sort the same objects using different rules
decisionPoints.ifNo: Start with obvious differences (big/small, red/blue) and model thinking aloud

closing.activity: Sorting explanations - students explain their sorting choices to partners and try to guess partners' sorting rules

troubleshooting.then: Provide sentence frames: 'I put these together because they are all...' or 'These go together because...'

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding how we organize things at home by putting similar items together, like toys in bins

lessons.title: Prédire et vérifier
lessons.oneGoal: Students will make simple predictions about what might happen and then test their ideas safely

opening.activity: Prediction demonstration - teacher models making a guess about what will happen, then testing it
opening.visualSupports: prediction process poster: guess, test, discover

main.activity: guided prediction and testing activities with safe materials like floating/sinking or rolling/sliding experiments
main.visualSupports: prediction vocabulary chart, testing safety reminders

decisionPoints.question: Are students making thoughtful predictions based on observations?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Have them explain why they made specific predictions
decisionPoints.ifNo: Model prediction thinking: 'I think this will float because it's light like...'

closing.activity: Prediction celebration - students share their favorite predictions and discoveries from testing

troubleshooting.then: Start with either/or choices: 'Do you think this will float or sink?' rather than open-ended questions

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding that we often guess what will happen before we try something, like predicting weather or game outcomes

lessons.title: Expérience simple avec l'eau
lessons.oneGoal: Students will conduct a safe, simple water experiment while following established safety and observation protocols

opening.activity: Water safety review and experiment preview - students practice safety rules and predict experiment outcomes
opening.visualSupports: water safety rules poster, experiment steps chart

main.activity: guided water experiment where students test objects for floating/sinking while using observation tools and recording results
main.visualSupports: experiment process chart, result recording template

decisionPoints.question: Are students following safety protocols and making good observations?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Let them design their own tests with additional objects
decisionPoints.ifNo: Provide more structure and model each step clearly

closing.activity: Experiment results sharing - students compare their discoveries and discuss surprises from the experiment

troubleshooting.then: Use simple pictures or stamps instead of writing: float symbol or sink symbol

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding that experiments help us learn by trying things safely, like testing which materials work best

lessons.title: Partager nos découvertes
lessons.oneGoal: Students will communicate their scientific observations and discoveries to classmates using words and drawings

opening.activity: Scientist presentation modeling - teacher demonstrates how scientists share discoveries clearly and excitedly
opening.visualSupports: good presentation rules poster with pictures

main.activity: student presentation preparation and practice where they choose their favorite discovery to share with the class
main.visualSupports: presentation planning template, audience listening rules

decisionPoints.question: Are students comfortable sharing their discoveries and findings?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage them to demonstrate their discoveries interactively
decisionPoints.ifNo: Allow sharing in pairs or small groups before presenting to the whole class

closing.activity: Discovery celebration - students applaud each presentation and share what they learned from classmates

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: speaking in front of the group
troubleshooting.then: Let them present to stuffed animals first or whisper their discovery to you to share

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding that scientists share their discoveries with others, like how we tell family about interesting things we learned

lessons.title: Scientifiques dans la nature
lessons.oneGoal: Students will apply their observation and safety skills to explore natural objects and phenomena outdoors (extension)

opening.activity: Outdoor safety preparation - reviewing safety rules for nature exploration and discussing what to observe outside
opening.visualSupports: outdoor safety rules poster, nature observation checklist

main.activity: guided outdoor exploration using learned observation skills to investigate natural objects, weather, and phenomena
main.visualSupports: portable observation guide, nature safety reminders

decisionPoints.question: Are students applying indoor observation skills successfully outdoors?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage them to make comparisons between indoor and outdoor discoveries
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on one observation skill at a time and provide more guided structure

closing.activity: Nature discoveries debrief - students share their most interesting outdoor observations back in the classroom

troubleshooting.then: Give specific challenges: 'Find something rough' or 'Listen for three different sounds'

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding that science happens everywhere, especially in nature where we can observe weather, plants, and animals

lessons.title: Questions de scientifiques curieux
lessons.oneGoal: Students will learn to ask scientific questions that can be investigated through safe observation and simple testing (extension)

opening.activity: Question modeling - teacher demonstrates asking scientific questions about classroom objects and how to find answers
opening.visualSupports: question word poster: What? How? Why? Where?

main.activity: guided question generation and simple investigation planning where students ask questions about familiar objects
main.visualSupports: question formation examples, investigation process chart

decisionPoints.question: Are students asking questions that can be answered through observation or simple testing?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Help them plan ways to investigate their questions safely
decisionPoints.ifNo: Model question formation and provide question starters: 'What happens if...' or 'How does...'

closing.activity: Question sharing circle - students share their scientific questions and discuss how they might find answers

troubleshooting.then: Start with wonder statements: 'I wonder what would happen if...' and turn them into questions

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding that asking questions leads to learning, just like how we ask questions to learn about new places or activities

lessons.title: Mini-laboratoire à la maison
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify safe science exploration opportunities they can pursue at home with family supervision (extension)

opening.activity: Home safety discussion - reviewing what makes science activities safe at home with family help
opening.visualSupports: home science safety rules poster with family pictures

main.activity: home science activity planning where students choose safe investigations they can do with family members
main.visualSupports: home science examples chart, family supervision reminders

decisionPoints.question: Can students identify which activities are safe for home exploration?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Help them plan specific home investigations with clear family instruction
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on simple observation activities that require no special materials

closing.activity: Home science promises - students commit to specific home explorations and discuss safety with families

troubleshooting.then: Create clear examples of DO and DON'T activities with pictures and simple rules

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding that science learning continues at home through safe kitchen experiments, nature walks, and careful observation

lessons.title: Aider les autres à être sécuritaires
lessons.oneGoal: Students will teach safety rules to younger students or family members, demonstrating their scientific safety knowledge (extension)

opening.activity: Teaching preparation - students review safety rules and practice explaining them simply to others
opening.visualSupports: teaching tips poster, safety rule visual aids

main.activity: safety teaching practice where students prepare presentations about science safety for younger students or families
main.visualSupports: good teaching examples, safety rule visuals for sharing

decisionPoints.question: Can students explain safety rules clearly and demonstrate them properly?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Have them create interactive safety demonstrations or games
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on one simple safety rule and model clear explanation techniques

closing.activity: Teaching reflection - students discuss how teaching others helps them remember safety rules better

troubleshooting.then: Practice with partners first and use simple phrases: 'Always remember to...'

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding that we can help keep others safe by sharing what we know, like teaching siblings about playground safety

lessons.title: Nos outils de scientifiques à la maison
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify common household items that can be used safely as science tools with adult supervision (extension)

opening.activity: Home tool hunt - students brainstorm household items that could work like science tools
opening.visualSupports: household science tools poster with pictures and safety notes

main.activity: home tool exploration where students match household items to science tools and plan safe home investigations
main.visualSupports: tool matching chart, home safety reminder posters

decisionPoints.question: Can students identify appropriate household items as science tools?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Have them plan specific investigations using these household tools
decisionPoints.ifNo: Show clear examples and focus on simple tools like measuring cups or flashlights

closing.activity: Home tool commitments - students choose specific household tools to use for science exploration with family

troubleshooting.then: Start with obvious examples like kitchen measuring tools or flashlights, then expand gradually

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding that science tools are all around us, like using kitchen measuring cups or flashlights for exploration

main.activity: science celebration showcase where students demonstrate skills, share discoveries, and teach visitors about safety

troubleshooting.then: Let them demonstrate with friends or focus on their strongest skills first

lessons.realWorldConnection: Sharing our scientific learning with families and showing how we can safely explore and discover the world around us

familyConnections.unitLetter:
Chers parents et familles,

Nous sommes ravis de commencer notre nouvelle unité: ""

Cette unité permettra à votre enfant de:
• Explorer des concepts importants en sciences
• Développer du vocabulaire en français
• Pratiquer de nouvelles compétences
• Faire des connexions avec la vie quotidienne

Quelques thèmes que nous explorerons:
Bienvenue dans notre laboratoire scientifique, Nos règles de sécurité en sciences, Observer avec nos yeux de scientifiques, Écouter comme des scientifiques, Sentir en sécurité

Comment vous pouvez aider à la maison:
• Demandez à votre enfant de partager ce qu'il/elle a appris
• Pratiquez le nouveau vocabulaire ensemble (voir la liste ci-jointe)
• Essayez les activités suggérées quand vous avez du temps
• Célébrez les efforts et les progrès, pas seulement les résultats

Encouragez les questions 'pourquoi' et explorez ensemble les réponses.
